answer: {arraySize: int, customizeCacheHolders:[{cacheValue (holder id), maxnodesCurrent:int, globalMaxnodes:str, localMaxnodes?, enableLocalMaxnodes?, timetoliveCurrent:int, globalTimetolive:str, loacalTimetolive?, enableLocalTimetolive?, maxageCurrent:int, globalMaxage:str, localMaxage?, enableLocalMaxage?, cacheEnable:str, cacheReadonly:str}]}
notes: Lab has 19 holders (Authorization.AdminLevelsCacheHolder, DirectoryService.UserCacheHolder, Workflow.Model.Process, RestAccess, …). The local time-to-live field is spelled 'loacalTimetolive'. Needs the cacheConfig page right.

purpose: Save per-holder cache settings.

fields.name: customizeCacheHolders[].cacheValue
fields.values: existing holder id from the GET

fields.name: customizeCacheHolders[].cacheEnable
fields.values: "true" keeps the holder enabled; anything else disables it (except read-only holders)

notes: DANGER: posting the GET answer back unchanged stopped the applications from starting after the next restart. The save writes a global property com.sssw.fw.cache.CacheHolderConfig:<holder> for every holder sent (in the User Application driver's cn=configuration,cn=AppDefs object), and for a read-only holder it always writes CacheHolder.active=true, whatever cacheEnable says. GlobalCacheHolder is read-only and had no such property; once written, the next start failed with 'ISPN000453: Attempt to define configuration for cache GlobalCacheHolder which already exists', the cache service did not start, and /IDMProv answered 404 everywhere. Restoring that object's XmlData from a copy taken before fixed it. So: send only the holders you change, never GlobalCacheHolder, and keep a copy of the configuration object. Per holder: unknown or blank cacheValue is reported as failed; omitting cacheEnable disables caching for that holder. The save also appends explicit zero values (MaxAgeSeconds=0, TimeToLiveSeconds=0) to holders that had none.

notes: Missing itemId or id is refused. Send the items flattened from itemCategories[].items and uncategorizedItems, each with its itemCategoryId. Only one of the two can be put back; the client view was restored.

purpose: List the workflow engines in the cluster with their state.
notes: engineState is a localised word (Running, Timedout, …). The lab shows two stale engine ids timed out next to the running one. Needs the workflow-engine page right. Each start of the applications adds a new engine id; earlier ids stay listed as Timedout or Shutdown. On the lab the engine's own cleanup of old timed-out engine ids failed every 2 minutes (a cleanup error repeated every 2 minutes), so they are never removed. After a stop and start over POST …/workflowengines/status, or a migration import, the running engine kept showing 'Starting' until the applications were restarted.

purpose: Read the workflow engine settings (thread pool, timeouts, intervals, process cache, heartbeat).
answer: {minPoolSize, maxPoolSize, initialPoolSize, keepAliveTime (s), userActivityTimeout, completedProcessTimeout, webServiceActivityTimeout, pendingInterval (s), cleanupInterval (h), retryQueueInterval (min), maxShutdownTime (min), enableEmailNotification, processCacheInitialCapacity, processCacheMaxCapacity, processCacheLoadFactor, heartbeatInterval (s), heartbeatFactor}
notes: Lab: pool 10/20/5, heartbeat 60 s x2. Lab has processCacheInitialCapacity 700 above max 500, which the save does not cross-check.

purpose: Save the workflow engine settings.
notes: Every field is read and range-checked, so send the full GET object back. Posting the GET answer back unchanged left it identical, including the lab's processCacheInitialCapacity 700 above processCacheMaxCapacity 500, which the save does not cross-check. Needs the workflow-engine page right.

purpose: Start or stop the workflow engine.
notes: engineStatus is fixed: 1 stops this server's workflow engine, 0 starts it; any other value or a missing one: 489 'invalid workflow status'. Stopping halts workflow processing until it is started again. The engine log showed STOPPING → STOPPED at once and STARTING → RUNNING within a second of the start, but GET …/workflowengines kept showing the engine as 'Starting' (the stored state was not updated after a start over REST; a restart of the applications brought a new engine id 'Running'). Open approval tasks survived. Provisioning administrator only (403). No dashboard call found.
